output.summary: An annual herb native across Europe, North Africa and Asia from Britain and the Canary Islands to Japan. Hooked hairs let its sprawling stems cling to plants and clothing, while its small fruits form adhesive burrs. Young leaves and stems can be cooked as a vegetable, and dried, roasted fruits have served as a lower-caffeine coffee substitute.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves and stems are cooked before fruits harden; dried, roasted fruits have often been used as a lower-caffeine coffee substitute.
